extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, patent drafters, inventors drafting claims
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on selecting and understanding transitional phrases in patent claims (e.g., 'comprising' vs 'consisting of') that determine claim scope and infringement coverage. Includes examples and discussion of combined/open/closed phrasing such as Markush groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of transitional phrases in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional phrases in patent applications specify whether the claim is limited to only the elements listed, or whether the claim may cover items or processes that have additional elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional wording is important because it determines claim scope (whether additional, unnamed elements are allowed). Choose transitional language deliberately to control breadth of coverage and potential infringement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-Ended ("comprising")
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of open-ended terms such as 'comprising' or 'which comprises' means that the claim encompasses all the elements listed, but may also include additional, unnamed elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If a claim recites elements 'A' and 'B', practicing the invention using 'A' and 'B' infringes, and using 'A', 'B', and an additional element 'C' also infringes. Example claim: 'A therapeutic composition comprising a polynucleotide having the sequence of SEQ ID NO:1.' These claims may be fairly broad, since any composition that has SEQ ID NO:1 within it would infringe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed-Ended ("consisting of")
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed-ended claim language such as 'consisting of' means that the composition (or device, or method) has the recited elements (or steps) and no more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A therapeutic composition consisting of a protein having the sequence of SEQ ID NO:2 and a suitable buffer.' This covers only the composition of SEQ ID NO:2 and the specified buffer; if any additional elements are added (not defined in the specification as part of the 'suitable buffer'), the composition would not be covered by that claim. Use 'consisting of' when a deliberately narrow, exclusive claim scope is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of open-ended and closed-ended language (Markush groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may combine open-ended and closed-ended language; e.g., an open-ended claim that incorporates a closed 'group consisting of' list (a Markush group) to specify alternatives while remaining open to additional elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A recombinant DNA construct comprising a polynucleotide selected from the group consisting of SEQ ID NO:1, SEQ ID NO:2, SEQ ID NO:3, SEQ ID NO:4, and SEQ ID NO:5.' Interpretation: the composition must contain at least one of the specified sequences but may also contain any number of additional, unnamed elements. This is an example of a Markush Group, common in the chemical arts.
